_risk_note: P1, raised from P2 by code review and owner ruling. level3-workflow.md:168 lists "destructive" under P1 and this slice's whole subject is a command that runs DROP DATABASE. The empirical case is the stronger one: four review rounds found four distinct ways the script could destroy the wrong database -- an unquoted identifier folded to another name, an over-long identifier truncated past its _test suffix, a fixed execution endpoint that ignored the URL's host, and query parameters that outranked the authority the guard checked. A P2 gate asks for one clean round; on this lane's own evidence one round would not have been enough.
_predecessor_note: Fifth registration, and the fourth caused by one missing capability rather than by any design question: an authorised change has no path into a hash-locked registration. v1 closed when a scoped file moved on origin/main. v2 closed because a P1 reclassification could not reach a hash-locked risk field. v3 closed by owner decision at 4/5 rather than spend the last round on a specifiable gap. v4 closed because a safety waiver the owner had WITHDRAWN on the merits remained the active text of negative_scope in both copies, where an underscore-keyed note could document the withdrawal but not perform it. No finding was ever contested; every one across all five lanes was accepted and fixed. Commits are carried by fast-forward from refs/archive/local-dev-sanctioned-paths--v4, identical objects.
_scope_note: docs/standards/kit-pack-membership.{json,md} are in scope because they are mechanically forced by the act of adding a file under scripts/, not because this lane wants to touch kit governance. check-kit-pack-membership.mjs enumerates scripts/ recursively (listScriptFiles) and auditCoverage reports any unclassified file as `missing`; `pnpm kit:check` is the FIRST command in `pnpm test`, so an unregistered new script turns the whole suite red. The .md is GENERATED -- `pnpm kit:generate` writes it and kit:check byte-compares it -- and is never hand-edited. Both new files are repo-owned by construction (absent from pack_pairs_verbatim), so each record carries overwrite_path `none`.
_invariant_note: test-chain is declared because registering scripts/db-reset-test.test.mjs into the `test:review-readiness` file list IS test-runner registration, which is that token's definition verbatim. It was tempting to declare build-config alone and call the package.json edit a manifest change; that would have been a dodge. v1 was refused on exactly this token while test-harness-chat-definer-lock-client-leak--v2 held it, and the refusal was correct on a second, independent ground the token could not have known: this script's DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) targets the same plexco_test that setupRlsTestContext opens as its admin connection, so running it during that lane's suite would have terminated their connection mid-run.
negative_scope: This field contains ONLY scope exclusions -- things this lane will not touch, and why. It contains NO decision rules. negative_scope is hash-locked at register AND compared between the authored and runtime copies, so anything written here costs a full close-and-re-register cycle to change. A decision rule is precisely the text that gets revised when review disagrees with it; putting revisable text in an immutable compared field guarantees that revising it costs a registration. That happened: a stopping rule lived here, review found it waived real defects, the owner withdrew it, and correcting it required this registration. Decision rules belong in the header of scripts/db-reset-test.mjs, where a commit corrects them.

_verification_note: Verification is scaled to a diff that contains zero TypeScript and zero product code. `pnpm -r run test` (the third leg of `pnpm test`) exercises packages this diff does not touch, needs a live Postgres, and is a measured flake source on a shared cluster. kit:check and test:review-readiness are both legs of `pnpm test` and both DO cover this diff: the first proves the two new scripts/ files are classified, the second proves the new test file is actually registered and RUNS rather than merely existing -- verify that property by checking the runner's total falls when scripts/db-reset-test.test.mjs is removed from the `test:review-readiness` list, not by comparing against a number written here. An earlier revision pinned 'from 85 to 91' and this lane's own next commit made it 93; the count is deliberately de-pinned rather than corrected, because correcting it only buys time until the next test is added. Full-suite verification belongs to merge time. The happy path WAS exercised once end to end on v2's equivalent tree: plexco_test was dropped and recreated, then the @plexco/db suite ran green on the rebuilt database (13 files, 716 tests), which is what proves recovery rather than mere deletion.

security_review.reason: MIRROR ONLY -- the primary copy of the threat model and every decision rule is the header of scripts/db-reset-test.mjs, because the gate builds its security prompt as a fixed string (autopilot-review-readiness.mjs:948-957) and never transmits this field; the reviewer sees only live source. Read the header. In brief: the script runs DROP DATABASE, so the trust boundary is everything that selects WHICH database dies. It defends against MISDIRECTION BY UNINTENDED LOCAL CONFIGURATION and not against an adversary already holding the host, the images or ~/.docker. Completeness is stated against the CALL PATH -- daemon, project, compose file, container, role, database -- because enumerating configuration is unbounded while the call path is bounded by the code. That list is a falsifiable hypothesis that keeps a refutation count, NOT a boundary on what counts as a defect: an in-model finding outside it must still be fixed. There is no shell-injection surface (spawnSync, argv array, no shell), and connection-string parsing is not an authority.

_manifest_sync_precondition: MANDATORY before the first `scope-gate ready` and again after any edit to this file: diff this authored contract against the runtime manifest at .autopilot/state/local-dev-sanctioned-paths--v5/manifest.json and PRINT the result -- a printed diff, not an assurance they match. Compare by exclusion: `jq 'walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(select(.key | test("^_") or . == "manifest_schema_version" or . == "review_gate_version" | not)) else . end) | .security_review.reason = null'` on both, then compare the two outputs.
_negative_scope_rule: negative_scope carries ONLY scope exclusions and their reasons -- never decision rules. It is hash-locked and compared, so its contents cost a registration cycle to change, and a decision rule is exactly the text review revises. Decision rules live in the header of scripts/db-reset-test.mjs.
